But I've always scooped boxes daily, 2x a day. What I've found is no litter box is large enough to go an entire day without scooping - even for 6 lbs cats. Worst part about this litter: the urine seeps to the bottom immediately - impossible to detect without scooping entire box… which in my case it had glued to the box… so maybe some kind of liner is needed. Ordered another that claims to be the softest, and more boxes to see which she prefers. For now, gone back to pre-moisten pellets, tho, there's plenty of this brand left, it'll wait until the extra boxes arrive. Always purchase unsented, your pets have far more sensitive noses than you.

reviews.title: Works well for elderly cat and automatic litterbox
reviews.text: My girl's pee smell was getting to be too much for me in my small townhome. My cat's area is in the room across from my bedroom. She is 14 and there is no way she is getting banished to the outdoors, so I had to find an alternative.  I am cursed with an above average olfactory system. I can't even wear perfume or be around people who have on strong perfume. Air fresheners and scented wall plugins are not an option for me. I've woken up from the smell of her litter box and got out of bed to go dump it out in the middle of the night. That's how bad it gets. So, I decided to get rid of her stainless steel box and bought an automatic litter box to help me keep her box clean right after she does her business so it doesn't have a chance to permeate the air for too long. That has helped but after several days the urine smell was back. I would have to completely empty out the box every week and start fresh. That was getting to be too expensive. I've had many brands of clay litter and none of them were effective. "10 days odor free" is a lie. Maybe 1 day tops. Also, her area is on the second floor so hauling up cases of clay litter was not fun. I saw an ad on Instagram for this litter so I decided to give it a try when I saw that Walmart carried it. I've been using it about a month now and I really am quite pleased with how it neutralizes odors. My cat took to it right away. I just mixed it in with her clay to get her adjusted and she was unbothered. I'm not going to say that it's perfect and I can't smell a thing, but it is far superior to any clay I have ever used. My office/cat space smells like the lumber aisle at a home improvement store now which I don't mind at all. I change out the bag that collects her used litter every other day and I don't really smell much urine anymore. The automatic litter box seems to handle it just fine. It does get stuck in certain places but it's easy to scrape off unlike clay. The clay was getting stuck in areas that would trip the sensor and prevent the box from completing its cleaning cycle. I am no longer having that issue. Anyway, the upstairs of my townhome smells good again and I can sleep in peace.

reviews.title: Catalyst is a Cata-YES!
reviews.text: I have been using regular clay scoopable cat litter since I've had cats. I've used every brand of it from scoop away to Walmart brand to Target brand. they're all good. they all do the same thing. Catalyst is different. it is a recycled or should I say upcycled soft wood? it's a natural clumping design and there are different formulas. the green bag has sent. the blue bag does not. I personally like the blue bag better. when I started using this I didn't think my cats were going to like it because it looks looks weird but they adapted to it really well. and as long as you follow the directions that are on the bag for acclimating to it, it works like a charm. all three of my cats have no problem with it. the best part is that you don't smell my cat litter anymore and the waist is much lighter because it's not a heavy clay and because it's made from wood compostable also. it will automatically degrade and it doesn't cause more landfill. it also lasts forever. apparently I bought one 35 lb bag about 2 months ago and I have three cats and I'm just finishing that first one and starting a new bag now. I was also transitioning so I did have previous cat litter in those boxes. now that I'm using it solely, I'll probably go through about a bag every 6 weeks, but that's way better than what I was doing before. it's much cheaper in the long run. I'm a happy cat mom with three content kitties. it also doesn't track very much as long as you use a mat around your litter box and it is dust free which is really nice. it's much better for my asthma. it also clumps into nice big clumps for urine purposes. I would suggest using a wire scoop instead of a plastic one. it makes it so it just pours through and you don't have to shake it.

reviews.title: Cata-horrible Cat Litter
reviews.text:
This is absolutely the worst cat litter I have ever used.  It is supposed to be clumping, but clumps immediately fall apart when scooping.  There is litter stuck in their paws and tracked all over the room.  The urine smell mixed with the wood smell is terrible.   Turds aren't a problem, but then unless they have diarrhea, it rarely is....

I honestly thought I got a defective  bag.  I went to their website and it states that if the litter is not clumping, it is too wet from humidity.  I live in SW Florida.  Humidity capital of the world.  The website states the litter doesn't track (it does) and that it absorbs odor (it does not).   I scoop daily, and use pan liners to keep the smell down.

On the up side (proverbial optimist) I only put the litter in one of the three litter boxes.  We have three kitties and three litter boxes.  I am so glad I didn't put it in the lanai box (12 feet from pool) or bedroom (OMG, hubby would have a fit if he walked through this mess barefoot).  Our kitties don't seem to mind it (two kittens 6 mos old and one senior grumpy cat).  

I have never purchased a product that was so completely off from the description.  I switched to avoid the dust and mess from clay litter, but I'm running back to Fresh Step and begging forgiveness.
